title: Changeset coverage is enforced, and a skip label releases the requirement
setupCommands: git init -b main -q && git add -A && git -c user.name=A -c user.email=a@a.dev commit -qm init && printf -- '\n// local edit\n' >> crates/core/src/lib.rs
expectation: A change under a package's path without a changeset is a policy failure, not a warning: `monochange affected --verify` exits nonzero and names the uncovered package. Adding release intent for that package satisfies the same command, so the check is about coverage rather than about the diff. A configured skip label releases the requirement without a changeset, which is how a maintainer marks a change as needing no release note.

checks.command: monochange affected --verify --changed-paths crates/core/src/lib.rs > .a.out 2>&1; rc=$?; grep -q 'changeset verification failed' .a.out; a=$?; grep -q 'acme-core' .a.out; b=$?; rm -f .a.out; test $rc -eq 1 -a $a -eq 0 -a $b -eq 0
checks.why: The gate that stops an uncovered change from merging. Both the failure and the package name must be present, because an agent recovers by reading which package it forgot.

checks.command:
mkdir -p .changeset; printf -- '---
acme-core: patch
---

Tighten the empty-document check
' > .changeset/grader.md; monochange affected --verify --changed-paths crates/core/src/lib.rs --changed-paths .changeset/grader.md > .a.out 2>&1; rc=$?; rm -f .changeset/grader.md .a.out; exit $rc
checks.why: The positive half: the same gate passes once the change is accompanied by release intent. Both paths must be passed because a changeset only counts when it is part of the change set being evaluated — it is the diff that carries it, which is how the check behaves in CI.

checks.command:
mkdir -p .changeset; printf -- '---
acme-cli: patch
---

Unrelated CLI fix
' > .changeset/grader.md; monochange affected --verify --changed-paths crates/core/src/lib.rs > .a.out 2>&1; rc=$?; rm -f .changeset/grader.md .a.out; test $rc -eq 1
checks.why: A changeset for a different package must not satisfy coverage for the changed one. Without this, the gate passes on any changeset at all and stops meaning anything.

checks.command:
cp monochange.toml .cfg.bak; printf '
[changesets.affected]
enabled = true
required = true
skip_labels = ["no-release-note"]
' >> monochange.toml; monochange affected --verify --label no-release-note --changed-paths crates/core/src/lib.rs > .a.out 2>&1; rc=$?; grep -q 'changeset verification skipped' .a.out; a=$?; mv .cfg.bak monochange.toml; rm -f .a.out; test $rc -eq 0 -a $a -eq 0
checks.why: The escape hatch a maintainer uses to mark a change as needing no release note. Pinning both the exit code and the skip message keeps the gate from becoming unconditional, which would push people to write meaningless changesets.
